title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dealer Transaction Anatomy Register
scope: Receiving-side archival controls that preserve multiple document types from natural-history dealer transactions. The register is a retrieval guide for recognising the paperwork expected around Blaschka orders: catalogues and price lists, correspondence, specimen/model lists, estimates, invoices, payment requests, bills of lading, postal receipts, account statements and shipping-insurance certificates.
evidence_guard: Most records below are not Blaschka transactions. Their purpose is to reconstruct the documentary anatomy of dealer-mediated scientific commerce so that missing or dispersed Blaschka transaction layers can be targeted systematically rather than inferred.

records.repository: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University Archives
records.reference: Conchological Section papers, Box 4 Folder 24, with adjacent financial series
records.evidence: The finding aid explicitly lists Damon's invoice for British shells and places dealer documents inside a broader receiving-side accounting archive.
records.research_value: Shows how a dealer invoice could be absorbed into institutional financial records that survive independently from the dealer's own papers.

records.evidence: The official inventory groups Ward correspondence concerning museum specimen purchases with requests for payment and bills of lading.
records.research_value: A compact receiving-side example in which sales, payment and freight paperwork survive together.

records.reference: SIA RU000208, Box 13 Folder 6; Series 5 Invoices, ca. 1867–1951
records.date_range: Ward file 1884, 1887–1895, 1899–1900, 1902–1904; invoice series begins ca.1867
records.evidence: RU000208 contains a dedicated Ward's Natural Science Establishment correspondence file. Its invoice series is described as divisional copies for specimen distribution recording specimen descriptions, catalogue numbers, collectors, localities and terms under which material was sent.
records.research_value: Provides a field schema for coding museum-side transaction documents. Even when a dealer letter is missing, invoice fields can preserve actor, object, place and transfer terms.
records.blaschka_guard: No Blaschka content is assigned to RU000208 without item-level inspection.

records.repository: American Museum of Natural History, Gottesman Research Library
records.evidence: The file documents negotiations for specimen purchases and preserves both cost estimation and account reconciliation alongside postal evidence.
records.research_value: Shows that the economic life of a dealer transaction could leave multiple records before and after payment, rather than a single invoice.

records.repository: American Museum of Natural History, Gottesman Research Library
records.evidence: The file groups specimen-sale correspondence with invoices and shipping-insurance certificates.
records.research_value: A later but unusually explicit control for the point at which object description, price and transit risk become separate documentary layers.

records.repository: American Museum of Natural History, Gottesman Research Library
records.evidence: The archival description identifies Ward price lists and catalogues kept together with correspondence.
records.research_value: Confirms that printed selection tools could remain attached to the correspondence they generated on the receiving side.

research_observation: A transaction should be reconstructed as a document bundle rather than as an invoice event. Different institutions often preserve different stages of the same commercial action. This provides a practical search template for Blaschka provenance: when one layer is present, adjacent record series should be checked for the missing selection, payment, freight, insurance and accession layers.
next_retrieval: Use the document-type vocabulary to recode existing Blaschka dealer cases and identify which transaction layers are genuinely absent versus merely unsearched.
For Ward, cross-check Rochester customer correspondence against receiving-side bills of lading and account statements.
For Damon, search customer financial series adjacent to known correspondence, not only name-indexed letters.
For Frič, inspect dealer-specific museum acquisition files for catalogues, quotations and receipts even when correspondence has not survived.
